title.en: New York Chinatown fears impact of $8bn casino development, calling it ‘predatory project’
title.zh: 纽约唐人街担忧80亿美元赌场开发项目的影响，称其为“掠夺性项目”

summary.en: Residents in New York's Chinatown express concerns over an $8 billion casino development, fearing it will exacerbate gambling addiction and drive up rents. Developers, however, highlight the potential for job creation.
summary.zh: 纽约唐人街的居民对一项80亿美元的赌场开发项目表示担忧，他们担心这会加剧赌博成瘾并推高租金。然而，开发商则强调该项目将创造就业机会。

body.en: Residents warn project could worsen gambling addiction and raise rents, while developers promise jobs On Main Street in Flushing’s Chinatown, shoppers weave between fruit stands, restaurants and family-run businesses that have served the New York City neighborhood for decades. But behind the bustle, many residents fear the working-class immigrant community is under threat from an $8bn casino development that could displace thousands of renters and force small businesses to close. “A predatory project is being dumped in our community that disproportionately harms our people,” said Jack Hu, 37, a Flushing resident and member of the No Casino in Flushing Meadows Corona Park campaign. “This community is really upset about this project and how it was pushed through without our consent.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 居民警告称，该项目可能会加剧赌博成瘾并提高租金，而开发商则承诺提供就业机会。在法拉盛唐人街的大街上，购物者穿梭于水果摊、餐馆和为纽约市社区服务了数十年的家族经营企业之间。但在喧嚣的背后，许多居民担心工薪阶层移民社区正受到耗资 80 亿美元的赌场开发项目的威胁，该项目可能会取代数千名租户，并迫使小企业关门。 37 岁的法拉盛居民、“法拉盛草原可乐娜公园禁止赌场”运动成员杰克·胡 (Jack Hu) 表示：“一个掠夺性项目正在我们的社区中倾倒，这对我们的人民造成了极大的伤害。” “这个社区对这个项目以及它是如何在未经我们同意的情况下进行的感到非常不安。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the tension between economic growth and community well-being, where the pursuit of wealth can bring both promised benefits and significant social costs. Yahweh reminds us that we cannot serve both God and Mammon, urging us to consider the true cost of our priorities.
reflection.zh: 这个故事凸显了经济增长与社区福祉之间的张力，对财富的追求既可能带来承诺的利益，也可能造成重大的社会代价。雅伟提醒我们不能既侍奉雅伟又侍奉玛门，敦促我们思考我们优先事项的真正代价。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

title.en: Most people arrested during Henry Nowak protests had been reported for domestic abuse
title.zh: 亨利·诺瓦克抗议活动中被捕的大多数人曾被举报有家庭虐待行为

summary.en: Police data in Hampshire, UK, revealed that a majority of individuals arrested during violent protests following a murder sentencing had prior reports or convictions for domestic abuse or intimate partner violence. Of 37 detained, 22 had such a history.
summary.zh: 英国汉普郡警方数据显示，在一名谋杀犯被判刑后发生的暴力抗议活动中被捕的大多数人，此前都有家庭暴力或亲密伴侣暴力的举报或定罪记录。在37名被拘留者中，有22人有此类历史。

body.en: Exclusive: Hampshire police data reveals 22 of 37 detained had been accused or convicted of intimate partner violence Most people arrested during violent protests after the sentencing of Henry Nowak’s murderer had previously been reported to the police for domestic abuse, the Guardian can disclose. Data released by Hampshire police under freedom of information laws shows that 22 of 37 people (59%) detained in Southampton after Vickrum Digwa was jailed for life have also been reported for crimes associated with intimate partner violence. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家：汉普郡警方数据显示，37 名被拘留者中，有 22 人被指控或被判犯有亲密伴侣暴力行为 据《卫报》透露，亨利·诺瓦克凶手被判刑后，在暴力抗议活动中被捕的大多数人此前都因家庭虐待向警方报案。汉普郡警方根据信息自由法公布的数据显示，维克鲁姆·迪格瓦被判终身监禁后，在南安普敦被拘留的 37 人中，有 22 人 (59%) 也因与亲密伴侣暴力相关的犯罪而被举报。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report highlights a disturbing link between public unrest and private violence, reminding us of the deep need for respect and honor within all relationships. Yahweh calls us to treat our partners with understanding and dignity, recognizing their equal worth as heirs of grace. When honor is absent in the home, it often reflects a broader disregard for...
reflection.zh: 这份报告揭示了公共骚乱与私人暴力之间令人不安的联系，提醒我们所有关系中都迫切需要尊重和尊荣。雅伟呼召我们以理解和尊严对待伴侣，承认他们作为恩典继承者的同等价值。当家庭中缺乏尊荣时，这往往反映出社会中对他人更广泛的漠视。

verse.textEn: Husbands, in the same way be considerate as you live with your wives, and treat them with respect as the weaker partner and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life.
verse.textZh: 你们作丈夫的，也要按情理和妻子同住；因她比你软弱，与你一同承受生命之恩的，所以要敬重她，这样便叫你们的祷告没有阻碍。

title.en: France evacuates Cap Ferret peninsula as Spain battles to prevent wildfires merging near Madrid – Europe live
title.zh: 法国疏散卡普费雷半岛，西班牙奋力阻止马德里附近野火蔓延——欧洲实时报道

summary.en: Wildfires are raging across parts of Europe, leading to mass evacuations in areas like France's Cap Ferret peninsula and threatening to merge near Madrid, Spain. Hundreds of boats and the sole road are being used to move residents to safety as dozens of fires continue to flare.
summary.zh: 欧洲部分地区野火肆虐，导致法国卡普费雷半岛等地大规模疏散，并威胁在西班牙马德里附近蔓延。数百艘船只和唯一一条道路被用于将居民转移到安全地带，数十处火灾仍在持续。

body.en: Evacuees have been told to leave using hundreds of mobilised boats or the only road linking the area with the mainland Over in France, it’s not just the south-west that gets affected, but the country’s south-east regions are also being hard hit, AFP noted. Dozens of fires flared up and are being fanned by the mistral wind around the historic village of Cotignac – officials saying around 25 houses had been destroyed since Tuesday. Continue reading...
body.zh: 法新社指出，撤离人员被告知使用数百艘动员的船只或连接该地区与大陆的唯一道路离开。在法国，不仅西南部受到影响，该国的东南部地区也受到严重打击。历史悠久的科蒂尼亚克村周围的密斯塔拉风助长了数十起火灾，官员称自周二以来约有 25 栋房屋被毁。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread wildfires forcing evacuations across Europe remind us of creation's deep groaning, as described in Romans 8:22. In these moments of environmental distress, we witness the vulnerability of both nature and human communities. Yet, even amidst such challenges, Yahweh's enduring presence offers a steadfast hope.
reflection.zh: 欧洲各地迫使民众撤离的野火，提醒我们罗马书8:22所描述的受造界深切的叹息。在这些环境困境中，我们看到自然界和人类社区的脆弱。然而，即使在这样的挑战中，雅伟永恒的同在也提供了坚定的盼望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Andy Burnham spends first working day at new No 10 North in Manchester – UK politics live
title.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 在曼彻斯特新的 No 10 North 度过了第一个工作日 – 英国政治直播

summary.en: PM, on his first day at new base, says it will create ‘that sense of a more balanced country, that big things can be done from here’ Andy Burnham has arrived by police convoy at No 10 North at Heron House in Manchester: Andy Burnham was probably feeling left out of the “Celtic...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Andy Burnham has defended the cost of opening No 10 North in Manchester, telling “London-based” critics that it’s better to have “a north pole that balances the south pole”.

Speaking to staff at the new centre, he said: “At least it creates that sense of a more balanced country, and that big things can be done from here.”

Heron House is temporarily accommodating No 10 North while a brownfield site just outside the city is being developed, where it is expected to relocate permanently once construction is complete.

As my colleagues Hannah Al-Othman and Priya Bharadia reported earlier this month , any “No 10” buildings “could be constructed without significant cost above that already signed off by the Treasury”.

Dai Davies, a former head of royal protection and a former divisional commander in the Metropolitan police, dubbed Burnham’s Manchester base as “Number 10A”.

“Number 10A will have to be strengthened,” he said, “and, of course, there’ll have to be a 24-hour-7 protection. So it’s going to cost us taxpayers millions in terms of technical security, surveillance, cameras.

“Depending on where it is, it may have to have underground detection systems, it probably will have to have a safe room, and Manchester police will have to bear the burden of protection, in the uniform sense, 24-7, I suspect. So the real cost is many millions of pounds.”
body.zh: 安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 为在曼彻斯特开设 No 10 North 的成本进行了辩护，他告诉“伦敦”的批评者，最好是“拥有一个平衡南极的北极”。 他对新中心的工作人员说：“至少它创造了一种更加平衡的国家的感觉，并且可以从这里做大事。” Heron House 暂时安置在 No 10 North，同时正在开发城外的棕地，预计施工完成后将永久搬迁。 正如我的同事 Hannah Al-Othman 和 Priya Bharadia 本月早些时候报道的那样，任何“10 号”建筑“都可以在不超出财政部已批准的成本的情况下建造”。 前皇家保护负责人、大都会警察局前分区指挥官戴戴维斯将伯纳姆的曼彻斯特基地称为“10A 号”。 “10A 号必须得到加强，”他说，“当然，还必须有 7 天 24 小时的保护。因此，在技术安全、监控和摄像头方面，我们纳税人将花费数百万美元。 “根据它所在的位置，它可能必须有地下探测系统，它可能必须有一个安全室，我怀疑曼彻斯特警方将必须承担统一意义上的保护负担，24小时7天。所以真正的成本是数百万英镑。”

title.en: South Africa's president wins bid to temporarily halt impeachment inquiry over 'Farmgate'
title.zh: 南非总统赢得暂时停止“农场门”弹劾调查的请求

summary.en: Ramaphosa has faced scrutiny following the theft of large sums of cash from his private farm in 2020.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A South African court has ruled in favour of President Cyril Ramaphosa's bid to temporarily halt a parliamentary inquiry looking into whether he should be impeached over what has been dubbed the "Farmgate" scandal.

In 2022, an independent panel said Ramaphosa might have a case to answer after burglars stole huge sums of cash, hidden in a sofa, from his private farm. The president denied any wrongdoing.

At the time MPs voted against establishing an impeachment inquiry, but in May the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had acted unlawfully by shelving the panel's report.

Ramaphosa is now challenging the findings of the panel in a separate court case to be heard in September.

The Constitutional Court's ruling in May paved the way for parliament to revive the impeachment process.

The make-up of parliament has radically changed over the last four years as Ramaphosa's African National Congress (ANC) party no longer holds a majority and governs as part of a coalition following the 2024 election.

The ruling by the Constitutional Court prompted the president to mount a legal challenge, saying the panel had "misconceived its mandate, misjudged the information placed before it and misinterpreted the four charges advanced against me".

On Friday, Western Cape high court judge Andre le Grange halted the parliamentary committee from proceeding with its hearings "pending the determination by this court of the applicant's review" - a reference to Ramaphosa's case against the panel.

The ruling effectively buys more time for Ramaphosa - time in which the president hopes he will be able to clear his name.

In court his legal team had argued that not halting the impeachment committee's work until his other case was ruled on could cause him irreparable reputational harm.

Three judges heard the matter: two ruled in his favour. The majority judgement means that until his other case is heard and finalised the impeachment proceedings cannot continue.

This whole saga goes back to 2020 when a robbery that took place at the president's private farm in Phala Phala, in Limpopo province.

Thieves broke in and stole money - at least $580,000 (£430,000) in US dollar bills - that had been stuffed into a sofa.

Details of the theft only came out two years later when the country's former spy chief, Arthur Fraser, highlighted the theft in an explosive dossier that he sent to the police.

Fraser, a close ally of Ramaphosa's predecessor Jacob Zuma, accused the head of state of hiding the theft from the police and tax authorities.

As the stolen cash was in foreign currency, it meant that exchange control laws could also have been contravened.

The president released a statement shortly after Friday's ruling saying he noted and "respects" the court's decision.

title.en: Tens of thousands evacuated from French tourist spot and near Madrid as wildfires spread
title.zh: 随着野火蔓延，数万人从法国旅游胜地和马德里附近撤离

summary.en: The fire has raged in the region for several days with officials now ordering the evacuation of the entire Cap Ferret peninsula.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
French authorities have ordered the evacuation of the entirety of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the south-west coast, with hundreds of people escaping the area by boat.

Tens of thousands of people are being evacuated from the tourism destination west of Bordeaux, as firefighters continue to battle what the local prefect has described as an "XXL fire" in the Gironde region.

The fires, which began on Tuesday, have burned for days, with officials saying 10,000 hectares (almost 25,000 acres) had been consumed by the flames.

Meanwhile, the government in Spain has declared a national emergency as wildfires burn out of control in several areas close to the capital Madrid.

Responding to the spread of fires, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, the president of the community of Madrid, said it was: "The worst fire in the history of the region."

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez spoke of a "dramatic situation" and urged people to take great care. Three fires were burning west of Madrid, at Villa del Prado and San Martín de Valdeiglesias.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 40,000 people had either been or were in the process of being evacuated from the Cap Ferret peninsula, which has the Atlantic on one side and the Bay of Arcachon on the other.

Local prefect Sophie Brocas said 53 homes had been lost as well as a campsite, but that 2,000 houses had been saved.

A local councillor said 2,000 evacuees from the peninsula had already arrived by boat in the port of Arcachon on the south side of the bay.

Fire and rescue chief Marc Vermeulen said the wildfire had spread rapidly at the end of Thursday and into the early hours of Friday. Authorities then took the decision on Friday morning to begin the evacuation of the town of Arès, which lies south-east of Lège-Cap Ferret on the Bay of Arcachon.

Vermeulen compared the fires overnight to those in 2022 - explaining the area is in a more severe state of drought now.

While in 2022, fires were "exploding" at the end of the day and the nights were favourable for firefighting, in the current fires they are exploding during the night at midnight or 01:00.

"When I say explosion, it means that for several hours, we had propagation speeds on the order of 800 to 1,000 hectares burned per hour, in the context of a suburban area."

Further down the Atlantic coast, around the town of Biscarrosse in France's Landes region, another major fire that began on Thursday afternoon has prompted the evacuations of more than 23,000 people.

About 18,000 people in Biscarrosse and 5,000 in Parentis-en-Born had to leave their homes, campsites, a nursing home and a summer camp.

title.en: Turkey: What chances does Ozel's new opposition party have?
title.zh: 土耳其：奥泽尔的新反对党有什么机会？

summary.en: After being removed as head of Turkey's main opposition CHP in May, Ozgur Ozel has announced the formation of a new party. Dozens of lawmakers have followed him, but will he be able to challenge President Erdogan?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After being removed as head of Turkey's main opposition CHP in May, Ozgur Ozel has announced the formation of a new party. Dozens of lawmakers have followed him, but will he be able to challenge President Erdogan?

In the early morning of May 24, shocking images of Ankara were broadcast around the world. After a court ordered that Ozel be ousted as head of the center-left Republican People's Party (CHP), the country's largest opposition party , its headquarters in the Turkish capital were surrounded by special forces .

The party leader and his allies had barricaded the doors with tables and chairs, but hours later they stopped resisting. "We want to avoid an escalation and are leaving of our own free will," a visibly shaken Ozel said. "Our only crime is to have defeated the ruling party."

Indeed, under his leadership, the CHP had managed something it had not succeeded in doing in 22 years. It had defeated the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) in a nationwide election.

In the local elections of March 2024, the party emerged as the strongest and took over control of city councils in 14 major cities. That included  Istanbul , whose mayor, Ekrem Imamoglu, quickly became so popular that he established himself as a serious challenger to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in the next presidential election, which is scheduled for 2028.

But soon Imamoglu was arrested , alongside several other mayors and their staff. They are accused of corruption and fraud. And then in May, Ozel was removed from his position .

Two months later, he announced the formation of the Yeni Parti , or "New Party," submitting formal registration to the interior ministry. With 91 lawmakers, it is set to become the second largest party behind the AKP in Turkey's 600-seat parliament.

Founded in 1923 by the founder of the Republic of Turkey , Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the CHP is Turkey's oldest political party, standing for the separation of church and state, patriotism and republicanism.

Ozel, who came from the pro-reform faction and became head in 2023, was able to open up the party to voters beyond its core base, placing more emphasis on the values of social democracy. He met with success, as the election results showed.

But after Ozel was ousted, Kemal Kilicdaroglu, the old party leader under whose watch the CHP had lost every election for two decades, returned. Kilicdaroglu was considered to be Erdogan's preferred opponent.

There has been much speculation as to why the party accepted the court ruling and agreed to the party being divided. Experts believe that behind the scenes, political calculations that benefit Erdogan are at play. The split will allow him to eliminate dangerous opponents ahead of the next presidential...
body.zh: 奥兹古尔·奥泽尔五月份被解除土耳其主要反对党共和人民党主席职务后，宣布成立一个新政党。数十名议员追随他，但他能挑战埃尔多安总统吗？ 5月24日凌晨，安卡拉令人震惊的画面在全世界播出。在法院下令罢免奥泽尔作为该国最大反对党中左翼共和人民党（CHP）主席后，该党位于土耳其首都的总部被特种部队包围。 该党领导人和他的盟友用桌椅挡住了门，但几个小时后他们停止了抵抗。 “我们希望避免事态升级，并自愿离开，”明显震惊的奥泽尔说道。 “我们唯一的罪行就是击败了执政党。” 事实上，在他的领导下，CHP 完成了 22 年来从未成功完成的事情。它在全国选举中击败了执政的正义与发展党（AKP）。 在2024年3月的地方选举中，该党成为最强党，并控制了14个主要城市的市议会。其中包括伊斯坦布尔，该市市长埃克雷姆·伊玛莫格鲁 (Ekrem Imamoglu) 很快就变得如此受欢迎，以至于他在定于 2028 年举行的下一届总统选举中成为土耳其总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安 (Recep Tayyip Erdogan) 的有力挑战者。 但很快伊玛莫格鲁与其他几位市长及其工作人员一起被捕。他们被指控腐败和欺诈。然后在五月，奥泽尔被免职。 两个月后，他宣布成立新党，并向内政部提交正式登记。该党拥有 91 名议员，将成为土耳其 600 席议会中仅次于正义与发展党的第二大党。 共和人民党于1923年由土耳其共和国创始人穆斯塔法·凯末尔·阿塔图尔克创立，是土耳其最古老的政党，主张政教分离、爱国主义和共和主义。 奥泽尔来自支持改革派，并于 2023 年成为党魁，他能够让该党向其核心基础之外的选民开放，更加强调社会民主主义的价值观。正如选举结果所表明的那样，他取得了成功。 但在奥泽尔被赶下台后，老党魁凯末尔·基里奇达罗格鲁（Kemal Kilicdaroglu）又回来了，在他的领导下，共和人民党在二十年来的每一次选举中都失败了。 基利奇达罗格鲁被认为是埃尔多安的首选对手。 对于该党为何接受法院裁决并同意分裂该党，外界有很多猜测。专家认为，在幕后，有利于埃尔多安的政治算计在起作用。这次分裂将使他能够在下一任总统之前消除危险的对手......

title.en: Why Trump's 'forced labor' tariffs leave the world puzzled
title.zh: 为什么特朗普的“强迫劳动”关税让世界感到困惑

summary.en: After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses. DW explains the new tariffs and the debate surrounding them.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses. DW explains the new tariffs and the debate surrounding them.

The Trump administration on Thursday announced new tariffs on 60 economies, including the European Union , citing their handling of imported goods made with forced labor .

In a statement, the United States Trade Representative (USTR) said it had investigated major trading partners and found that they failed to impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods made through modern slavery.

The tariffs cover more than 99% of US imports  and replace a temporary 10% global tariff that was due to expire.

A 10% tariff will apply to countries like Argentina, India, Pakistan and the UK that have adopted or committed to forced-labor import restrictions.  

The EU, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Switzerland will face tariffs of either 10% or 12.5%, depending on the product.

Goods from 38 other countries will be subject to the higher tariff of 12.5%, including China , most of the Middle East, much of Latin America, Australia, New Zealand and Russia.

Exemptions include steel, aluminum, automobiles, civilian aircraft, rare earth minerals and goods covered by the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement .

The new tariffs took effect just after midnight Eastern Standard Time on Friday, July 24.

The USTR noted that the US has banned imports made with forced labor for almost a century, adding that despite international consensus, "the prevalence of forced labor persists worldwide and has even escalated in recent years."

Washington argues that foreign producers gain an unfair price advantage from the practice and that US workers cannot compete with forced-labor wages.

In reality, many critics and analysts see the move as a legal workaround for US President Donald Trump's broad tariff program, announced on "Liberation Day" April 2, 2025, which the US Supreme Court struck down in February.

At that time, Trump invoked the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) of 1977 to impose the tariffs without congressional approval, but the court ruled that the law does not authorize presidents to impose tariffs on their own.

The new forced labor tariffs were introduced under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a more established trade law that many analysts believe will be harder for courts to overturn.

Compared with parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America, forced labor isn't a major issue within the 27-member EU, due to comprehensive labor laws and strong enforcement.

body.zh: 在美国最高法院驳回唐纳德·特朗普的紧急关税后，白宫转向另一项与涉嫌侵犯人权有关的贸易法。德国之声解释了新关税以及围绕它们的争论。 特朗普政府周四宣布对包括欧盟在内的 60 个经济体征收新关税，理由是这些经济体对强迫劳动制造的进口商品的处理方式。 美国贸易代表（USTR）在一份声明中表示，它已经对主要贸易伙伴进行了调查，发现他们未能实施并有效执行禁止进口通过现代奴隶制制造的商品。 这些关税涵盖了超过 99% 的美国进口产品，并取代了即将到期的 10% 临时全球关税。 10%的关税将适用于阿根廷、印度、巴基斯坦和英国等已经采取或承诺限制强迫劳工进口的国家。 欧盟、台湾、日本、韩国和瑞士将面临 10% 或 12.5% 的关税，具体取决于产品。 来自其他 38 个国家的商品将被征收 12.5% 的较高关税，其中包括中国、中东大部分地区、拉丁美洲大部分地区、澳大利亚、新西兰和俄罗斯。 豁免包括钢铁、铝、汽车、民用飞机、稀土矿物以及美国-墨西哥-加拿大协议涵盖的商品。 新关税于 7 月 24 日星期五东部标准时间午夜过后生效。 美国贸易代表办公室指出，美国近一个世纪以来一直禁止进口强迫劳动产品，并补充说，尽管国际社会达成共识，“强迫劳动现象在世界范围内仍然普遍存在，而且近年来甚至有所升级。” 华盛顿认为，外国生产商从这种做法中获得了不公平的价格优势，而美国工人无法与强迫劳动的工资竞争。 事实上，许多批评者和分析人士认为此举是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在 2025 年 4 月 2 日“解放日”宣布的广泛关税计划的法律解决方案，美国最高法院于 2 月份驳回了该计划。 当时，特朗普援引1977年《国际紧急经济权力法》(IEEPA)在未经国会批准的情况下征收关税，但法院裁定该法律并未授权总统自行征收关税。 新的强迫劳动关税是根据 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条引入的，这是一项更为成熟的贸易法，许多分析人士认为法院更难推翻该法。 与非洲、亚洲和拉丁美洲部分地区相比，由于劳动法全面且执法力度强，强迫劳动在欧盟 27 个成员国中并不是一个主要问题。 国际劳工组织 (ILO) 将强迫劳动定义为在惩罚和……威胁下进行的工作。

summary.en: The meeting came hours after activist Sonam Wangchuk announced he was ending his 26-day hunger strike.

body.en:
Thousands of people continue to protest demanding the Indian education minister's resignation after representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held talks with the government.

CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka told reporters that the government has asked for a day to decide on their biggest demand - minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

"The protest will continue and will keep growing until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns. If that does not happen soon, we will be forced to announce another nationwide protest call," said Ranka.

The protests, which began more than a month ago, gained momentum this week after a police crackdown on people marching to parliament left dozens injured .

The protests are led by CJP, an online satirical movement that has evolved into a powerful platform for young people's anxieties and dissent.

Saurav Das, another CJP spokesperson, said the government had responded positively to two other demands: compensation for the families of students who reportedly died by suicide after the cancellation of a major medical entrance exam in May, and the withdrawal of police cases against protesters who joined the march to parliament. He said the two sides would meet again on Saturday.

Federal minister JP Nadda told reporters that the government would inform CJP on Saturday "about the discussion we had among the government".

The meeting followed an eventful night where activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after 26 days of fasting in solidarity with the protests.

A short while before that, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also posted a video promising a tough new law on examination paper leaks, the issue at the core of the protests.

The protests have become a major headache for Modi's government, which had tried to ignore them in the first few weeks.

That changed last Saturday, when authorities forcibly removed Wangchuk from the protest site and admitted him to hospital, citing health concerns.

Two days later, police in Delhi cracked down on protesters attempting to march to parliament, sparking massive public anger.

On Thursday night, Modi posted a video message - shot vertically, seen as an attempt to reach the young protesters who are active on Instagram - saying that a tough new law on examination paper leaks was being prepared.

He said he had received a draft of the law, which they wanted to introduce soon in parliament.

Exam paper leaks are at the centre of the controversy - India has witnessed dozens of them over the past couple of decades. The latest trigger was the leak of the question paper for the medical entrance exam, National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).

Nearly 2.28 million candidates sat the exam on 3 May. It was cancelled days later, and a re-test was held .

title.en: Flaming teacakes, bedazzled unicorns: The Commonwealth Games' surprises unpacked
title.zh: 燃烧的茶饼，令人眼花缭乱的独角兽：英联邦运动会的惊喜揭晓

summary.en: Three years after Victoria abandoned hosting the Commonwealth Games, the sporting extravaganza has opened in Glasgow.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Head of the Commonwealth emerging from a time-travelling blue box, unicorns prancing on stage, and fire spurting from an oversized teacake.

Those were the scenes at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Friday morning.

Victoria was initially meant to host the games, but withdrew in 2023 due to soaring costs.

Glasgow, which previously hosted the event in 2014, stepped in to save it — and brought their finest, most-bedazzled unicorns to mark the occasion.

This year's Commonwealth Games is running on a bare-bones budget, arriving at a time when people have questioned their relevance, particularly following the Victorian government's withdrawal.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

But despite the troubles, Friday's ceremony was a party — with scenes that looked like they could have been plucked from vivid dreams.

One of the most unique scenes from Friday morning was the image of King Charles and Queen Camilla emerging from a very large TARDIS — the name for the time machine in the long-running British sci-fi television show, Doctor Who.

Gasps and cheers came from the crowd as the royal couple appeared on a stage that transformed into a magic garden.

Scotland's largest city welcomed able-bodied and para-athletes from 74 competing nations, including a third of Australia's 257-strong team who were part of the procession.

It's not the first time a monarch has appeared at a similar event. For the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics, Queen Elizabeth II appeared to skydive into the stadium alongside Daniel Craig, James Bond-style.

In Glasgow, the UK's new prime minister Andy Burnham was also in attendance, alongside Scotland's First Minister John Swinney and the First Minister of Wales Rhun ap Iorwerth.

The opening ceremony traversed through many facets of Glasgow's history and culture, starting with a day in the life of the industrial city, pictured under its famous Glasgow Central Station clock.

The flashmob soon descended into a bizarre fever dream, where dancing unicorns with traffic cones paid tribute to the city's underground club culture.

For decades, traffic cones have been regularly placed on an equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington and remain a symbol of Glaswegians' resistance to authority.

The unicorn is both a nod to the playful tradition and the creature being the national animal of Scotland since the 1300s.

There were also plenty of cameos and performances, including from a range of Scottish celebrities.

body.en:
Wildfires sweeping through parts of Italy, France and Spain on Thursday forced thousands of people to flee blazes fanned by scorching temperatures and strong winds.

Thousands of tourists on France's southern Atlantic coast have been forced out of campsites and holiday homes while Spanish authorities ordered another town near Madrid to evacuate late Thursday because of an out-of-control forest fire.

Three firefighters have been killed as southern Europe endures more severe heat, with temperatures topping 40C in some areas.

The total area of land burnt so far this year in European Union countries is the second largest on record, according to satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards and civil protection officers battled dozens of fires, some raging for several days, across the Italian island. One firefighter died after falling ill while battling the flames, the interior minister said.

"We were on the beach and they told us to go back to the campsite to collect our things," said Belgian tourist Elke Urbain.

"We're not afraid because everyone is taking care of us, but we're sad for the people here."

Skies over Le Porge turned orange as smoke rose from charred and crackling pine trees, while helicopters made repeated runs over evacuated neighbourhoods.

Fires in 2022 damaged 30,000 hectares of the same forest, forcing some 50,000 people to be evacuated.

Fires are breaking out faster because of climate change caused by the burning of oil, coal and gas. European droughts are now more severe, climatologists from the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published on Thursday.

Across the border in Spain, authorities ordered 3,500 people in a town west of Madrid to leave their homes late Thursday because of a forest fire burning out of control.

Emergency services said alert messages had been sent to people in Aldea de Fresno ordering their evacuation.

title.en: Trump's Israel condition throws Saudi Arabia nuclear deal into doubt
title.zh: 特朗普就以色列问题设条件，沙特核协议前景不明

summary.en: The White House has stated that any nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia is contingent on the kingdom formally recognizing Israel.
summary.zh: 白宫表示，沙特阿拉伯必须承认以色列，否则与沙特的核协议将无法达成。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump said a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognising Israel — casting uncertainty over the agreement just the day after it was signed.

Saudi Arabia has long resisted joining the Abraham Accords , under which several Arab states established ties with Israel. The kingdom has long rejected joining the accords in the absence of a pathway toward Palestinian statehood.

The civilian nuclear deal announced on Thursday had appeared to be a major win for the Saudis, especially coming as Trump wages war on Iran in large part over concerns about the country's own atomic program.

But Trump threw a spanner into the works with his post on his Truth Social network saying the Saudi deal "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords".

The White House said that the Saudis knew the deal was contingent on recognising Israel, although it was not mentioned when the deal was announced.

"The president is always the final dealmaker, as you know," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt told reporters, adding that the Abraham Accords were "something that he feels very strongly about and has spoken about it in the past and will continue to uphold".

She said the US would "continue to have those conversations with our Saudi counterparts" to finalise a deal including recognition of Israel.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said recognition by Saudi Arabia, a regional power and home to Islam's holiest sites, would mark a "historic leap" forward for peace in the Middle East.

Leavitt said she did not know of any calls between Trump and Netanyahu following the announcement of the Saudi agreement.

Should it go through, the deal to establish a civilian nuclear program in Saudi Arabia would generate billions of dollars for US companies, but with Trump's latest announcement, it was unclear whether it would ever see the light of day.

HA Hellyer, a senior associate fellow at the United Kingdom-based think tank the Royal United Services Institute for Defence and Security Studies, said if the US "tries to force normalisation on Riyadh, it's not likely to work out very well".

"Would Saudi decide to do a complete 180 on what it has declared for the past three years, or 30 years? Quite dubious," he said.

Critics have also insisted that the deal could precipitate a nuclear race in a region already battered by war.

One provision would potentially see US companies build a uranium enrichment facility in Saudi Arabia, The Wall Street Journal reported.

title.en: The US' $166 billion refund comes with a much bigger cost
title.zh: 美国1660亿美元的退款代价更高昂

summary.en: Trump's willingness to use tariffs to create persistent uncertainty signals a greater economic and legal danger.
summary.zh: 特朗普愿意利用关税制造持续的不确定性，这预示着更大的经济和法律风险。

body.en:
An Australian clothing company, Nashie, recently received a six-figure refund from the US government, including 6 per cent interest, for tariffs it had paid on US imports. It’s just one of thousands of businesses reclaiming tariffs imposed on what President Donald Trump called "Liberation Day".

Of the roughly US$166 billion (AU$237 billion) due to be refunded, more than US$85 billion (AU$121 billion) has already been returned to businesses.

But while a US Supreme Court ruling in February reversed the tariffs, much of the economic and political damage, and perhaps some of the Trump administration’s gains, will be hard to undo.

Trump’s April 2025 tariffs relied on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law that lets presidents respond to extraordinary foreign threats — yet never mentions the word "tariff".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

On 20 February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled in a 6-3 decision that IEEPA did not authorise tariffs — under the Constitution, only Congress has the power to impose taxes and duties.

The decision placed an important limit on the president’s power to impose tariffs. But it did not end Trump’s tariff policy, which was, from the beginning, designed to buy time to rewrite US trade relations with the rest of the world.

Trump responded with a temporary 10 per cent global tariff, which expires on 24 July after the statutory 150-day limit.

Trump has also pursued more targeted tariffs under laws dealing with unfair trade practices, national security and anti-slavery claims.

These require investigations into foreign trade practices and lengthy procedures, which slow the process and also create a record that can be scrutinised in court.

The US Trade Representative’s findings on alleged forced labour have prepared the ground for a 12.5 per cent tariff on exports from 54 countries, including Australia, China, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, starting on 24 July 2026.

So while the Supreme Court closed one legal door, the Trump administration was already preparing to walk through another. And it has bought itself yet more time.

The refunds paid out contributed to a US$120 billion (AU$171 billion) federal deficit this June, in sharp contrast to the US$27 billion (AU$38 billion) surplus in June 2025.

That said, the US$166 billion (AU$236 billion) being paid out is not a fine. Much of it is money the government collected without legal authority and must now return. This is real money, but it’s less than 2 per cent of the projected 2026 federal government spending.

title.en: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
title.zh: 瑞典放宽采矿许可，以减少对中国矿产的依赖

summary.en: Sweden has designated the mining of critical minerals and rare earths as a national security interest. This move aims to simplify and accelerate the permit process for mining, with the government stating it is necessary to reduce the country's reliance on China for these resources.
summary.zh: 瑞典已将关键矿产和稀土的开采定为国家安全利益。此举旨在简化和加快采矿许可程序，政府表示此举是为了减少对中国的依赖。

body.zh: 瑞典已宣布关键矿物和稀土的开采属于国家安全利益。这将简化并加快许可流程。政府表示，需要采取这一措施来对抗对中国的依赖。 瑞典周四宣布了计划，试图推动其采矿业，特别是稀土行业，并对抗欧洲对中国的依赖。 资源丰富的瑞典已经成为欧洲最大铁矿的所在地，并在基律纳的同一北极圈地点发现了大量稀土矿藏。 稀土矿物对于可再生能源发电、国防和电动汽车生产、现代计算机制造和其他核心产业至关重要。中国约占全球采矿和炼油业的70%。 斯德哥尔摩政府周四宣布，关键金属和稀土矿物的开采符合国家安全利益。 兼任副总理的能源部长埃巴·布希 (Ebba Busch) 表示，这应该会简化和加快新开采项目的许可流程，并有助于吸引投资。 “瑞典必须成为领先的矿业国家，”她在概述新战略时表示，政府打算“简化授权程序，以便更快地做出决定。” 布希表示：“我们相信，这可以对瑞典、欧盟和北约的防御能力做出重大贡献。”他称欧洲工业对中国的依赖是一种“系统性风险”。 布施还表示，此举将使国家更容易为采矿项目分配土地，这是一个与放牧驯鹿的萨米原住民关系紧张的领域，他们表示采矿业的扩张可能意味着他们传统生活方式的终结。 能源部长还表示，政府正在考虑为采矿业设立一家国有投资公司。 她说：“今天，坦白地说，政府缺乏具体工具来明智地促进关键战略项目的加速和吸引投资。” 自 10 世纪和大型法伦铜矿开采以来，瑞典一直是欧洲矿业巨头，该矿一度生产了欧洲大陆三分之二的铜。该国许多房屋、教堂和其他建筑物所装饰的独特深红色被称为法轮红，来自废弃的矿山。它现在是一个博物馆和联合国教科文组织世界遗产。 瑞典现代的法伦是位于北极圈基律纳的巨大LKAB铁矿。瑞典拥有欧洲约 60% 的已知铁矿石储量，截至 2021 年，瑞典开采了欧洲大陆约 90% 的铁矿石，其中仅基律纳就占了约三分之一。 广阔的...

reflection.en: Nations often face complex decisions to ensure their long-term stability and security. This strategic move by Sweden highlights the importance of wise guidance in national planning, ensuring a people's safety and reducing vulnerabilities. It reminds us that thoughtful leadership, seeking sound counsel, is vital for navigating an interconnected world.

title.en: US-Saudi nuclear deal: How will it impact Middle East, US-Iran war?
title.zh: 美国-沙特核协议：将如何影响中东和美伊战争？

summary.en: Critics warn that a potential US-Saudi nuclear deal could ignite a nuclear arms race in the Middle East, causing concern among US allies like Israel and the UAE. Reports suggest the US may be reconsidering aspects of the agreement.
summary.zh: 批评人士警告称，一项潜在的美国与沙特核协议可能在中东引发核军备竞赛，这已引起美国盟友如以色列和阿联酋的不安。有报道指出，美国可能正在重新考虑该协议的某些方面。

body.en:
Critics say the US-Saudi deal could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. It's certainly not making US allies, like Israel and the UAE, happy. And reports suggest the US may already be backtracking on the deal.

After new statements by US President Donald Trump on Thursday morning, it is still unclear whether a controversial new deal with Saudi Arabia that allows the Middle Eastern autocracy to establish a civilian nuclear program will go ahead.

Trump said the deal could only progress if Saudi Arabia normalized diplomatic relations with Israel. In the recent past, the Saudi government has repeatedly stated it would only do this if the Israelis make genuine moves toward establishing a Palestinian state. With the current Israeli government, that is unlikely to happen.

The deal must also be voted on by the US Congress and there's been backlash already, with critics saying it could set off a nuclear arms race in the Middle East.

One of the main reasons experts are so worried is that in several years' time, the deal, as it stands now, may let the Saudis enrich their own uranium. The more uranium is enriched, the more it could potentially be diverted to make weapons. And in the past Saudi Arabian ruler Mohammed bin Salman has said that if Iran produces a nuclear bomb, then Saudi Arabia would need to have one too. 

The majority of the approximately 38 countries with civilian nuclear energy programs don't enrich uranium. Instead they import it.

The US-Saudi deal also has regional implications, especially because it seems to have been formulated in a far less rigorous way than similar deals.

The less strict deal the US has made with Saudi Arabia is likely to upset the  United Arab Emirates , who often compete with the Saudis for geopolitical influence.

The UAE already has a nuclear power plant, Barakah, as a result of arrangements made with the Americans back in 2009. 

As with almost all of the 26 nuclear cooperation agreements the US has, the UAE's deal also included what's known as an "additional protocol" signed with the International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA. This means the IAEA can thoroughly inspect all nuclear facilities. The UAE also agreed to forgo uranium enrichment.

The Saudi deal is bilateral only — that is, just between the US and the Saudis and doesn't include the IAEA — and the Saudis may eventually be allowed to enrich their own uranium.

body.zh: 批评人士称，美国与沙特的协议可能引发中东核军备竞赛。这肯定不会让以色列和阿联酋等美国盟友感到高兴。有报道称，美国可能已经在该协议上撤回。 在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周四上午发表新声明后，目前尚不清楚与沙特阿拉伯达成的一项有争议的新协议是否会继续进行，该新协议允许中东独裁政权建立民用核计划。 特朗普表示，只有沙特阿拉伯与以色列实现外交关系正常化，该协议才能取得进展。最近，沙特政府一再表示，只有以色列真正采取行动建立巴勒斯坦国，沙特才会这样做。对于现任以色列政府来说，这种情况不太可能发生。 该协议还必须由美国国会投票表决，并且已经引起了强烈反对，批评者称这可能引发中东核军备竞赛。 专家们如此担心的主要原因之一是，几年后，按照目前的协议，沙特可能会浓缩自己的铀。铀浓缩得越多，就越有可能被转用于制造武器。沙特阿拉伯统治者穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼过去曾表示，如果伊朗生产核弹，那么沙特阿拉伯也需要拥有一枚。 大约 38 个拥有民用核能计划的国家中的大多数国家不进行铀浓缩。相反，他们导入它。 美国与沙特的协议也具有区域影响，特别是因为它的制定方式似乎远不如类似协议那么严格。 美国与沙特阿拉伯达成的不那么严格的协议可能会让阿拉伯联合酋长国感到不安，因为阿联酋经常与沙特争夺地缘政治影响力。 由于 2009 年与美国达成的安排，阿联酋已经拥有巴拉卡核电站。 与美国签署的几乎所有 26 项核合作协议一样，阿联酋的协议还包括与国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 签署的所谓“附加议定书”。这意味着国际原子能机构可以彻底检查所有核设施。阿联酋还同意放弃铀浓缩活动。 沙特协议只是双边协议——也就是说，仅在美国和沙特之间达成，不包括国际原子能机构——沙特最终可能被允许浓缩自己的铀。 努尔·艾德今年早些时候告诉德国之声，对阿联酋来说，核电更多的是作为第一个开发核电的阿拉伯国家的声誉，而不是军事野心。 Eid 是一位驻巴黎的独立研究员，他为许多思想家发表了有关中东核野心的论文......

title.en: Weather tracker: More than 900 wildfires rage across Canada
title.zh: 天气追踪：加拿大900多处野火肆虐

summary.en: More than 900 wildfires are currently burning across Canada, with many out of control in the Northwest Territories and Ontario. Recent hot, dry weather has contributed to the fires, which have already scorched approximately 3 million hectares.
summary.zh: 加拿大目前有超过900处野火正在燃烧，其中西北地区和安大略省的许多火势仍未得到控制。近期炎热干燥的天气助长了火势，已烧毁约300万公顷土地。

body.en: Fires remain out of control in Northwest Territories and Ontario, while Argentina endures record night-time heat Recent hot, dry weather in Canada has triggered hundreds of wildfires across the country. As of Wednesday, more than 900 were burning, scorching about 3m hectares of land. While fires have broken out in several provinces, the greatest concern is in the Northwest Territories and Ontario , where several remain out of control. Poor air quality has been reported across affected regions, with wildfire smoke carried by winds into the US and even across the Atlantic to northern Europe. The risk of further blazes remains high as North America enters the peak of fire season. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The widespread wildfires across Canada, consuming millions of hectares, remind us of creation's deep vulnerability and its 'groaning' under the weight of environmental distress. In these moments of ecological crisis, we are called to lament with the Earth and seek ways to care for the world Yahweh has entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 加拿大各地蔓延的野火吞噬了数百万公顷土地，这提醒我们受造界的脆弱，以及它在环境困境重压下的“叹息”。在这些生态危机时刻，我们受召与大地一同哀叹，并寻求方法来照管雅伟托付给我们的世界。

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

reflection.en: In a world of intense technological competition and rising international tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people becomes profoundly relevant. Even amidst accusations and threats, seeking paths to de-escalation and mutual respect is vital for global stability. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to pursue peace wherever possible, even when faced with...
reflection.zh: 在科技竞争激烈、国际关系日益紧张的世界中，与所有人和平相处的呼召变得至关重要。即使面对指控和威胁，寻求缓和局势和相互尊重的途径对全球稳定也至关重要。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们，即使面对竞争，也要尽可能追求和平。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Democratic lawmakers propose bank funded by China tariffs to boost US manufacturing
title.zh: 民主党议员提议设立由对华关税资助的银行以提振美国制造业

summary.en: Democratic lawmakers have proposed creating a bank, funded by tariffs on China, to provide grants, loans, and investments for US manufacturing. This initiative aims to revitalize the country's industrial heartlands and support smaller businesses.
summary.zh: 民主党议员提议设立一家由对华关税资助的银行，旨在为美国制造业提供拨款、贷款和投资。这项举措旨在振兴美国的工业腹地并支持小型企业。

body.en: Exclusive: Ro Khanna says ‘reindustrialization’ effort would provide grants, loans and investments to smaller businesses Democrats in the US Congress have laid out plans for what they say would be the “boldest” bid to revitalize the country’s industrial heartlands since the second world war – using revenue raised by tariffs on China. A bill introduced this week would create a new bank to strengthen domestic manufacturing, provided with up to $15bn in funds each year. Continue reading...
body.zh: 独家报道：罗·卡纳表示，“再工业化”努力将为小型企业提供赠款、贷款和投资。美国国会的民主党人已经制定了计划，他们称这是自二战以来“最大胆”的振兴美国工业中心地带的计划——利用对中国征收关税获得的收入。本周提出的一项法案将创建一家新银行来加强国内制造业，每年提供高达 150 亿美元的资金。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As lawmakers propose strategies to boost national manufacturing and economic strength, it is a reminder that Yahweh is the one who gives us the ability to produce wealth. This divine provision calls us to steward our economic endeavors with wisdom and purpose, recognizing that true prosperity ultimately comes from Him.
reflection.zh: 当议员们提出振兴国家制造业和经济实力的策略时，这提醒我们，是雅伟赐予我们创造财富的能力。这种神圣的供应呼召我们以智慧和目标来管理我们的经济事业，认识到真正的繁荣最终来自祂。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: Blocked by censors, China's animal lovers take fight against abuse offline and overseas
title.zh: 遭审查阻挠，中国动物爱好者将反虐待斗争转至线下和海外

summary.en: The killing of a dog and her puppies in Guangdong, China, has provoked widespread outrage both within the country and internationally. Animal welfare advocates, facing censorship, have taken their campaign against animal abuse offline and sought support overseas.
summary.zh: 中国广东省一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的事件，在中国国内外引发了广泛的愤怒。面对审查，动物福利倡导者已将他们的反虐待动物运动转至线下并寻求海外支持。

body.en:
When videos showing the horrific killing of a stray dog and her puppies sparked outrage on the Chinese internet in June, Beijing's censorship machine kicked into action.

But what was unusual this time was that it pitted the shocked and angry voices against authorities who said they were concerned about the four boys involved, all of them younger than 14.

China's Communist Party regime tightly controls media and the internet to suppress criticism of the state and to manage public anger. But in this case authorities cited the age of the boys as they urged people to withhold their comments and scrubbed social media posts about the incident.

"We urge the public not to disseminate related information, to reject cyberbullying, and to work together to create a good environment for the growth of minors," reads an official statement.

But the restrictions only seemed to spur the outcry. China's animal lovers have now taken their fight offline and abroad, even putting up billboards in New York to drum up support.

In China, posts about the incident are still drawing thousands of comments across social media, three weeks after the incident. There is shock, anger and sorrow, as well as demands for laws against animal cruelty, which China currently does not have.

Disturbing footage showing the boys in the city of Jieyang, Guangdong province, hitting three puppies with sticks before setting their mother on fire emerged online at the end of June. The boys were seen laughing as the dog, named Wang Wang, burned.

Jieyang authorities said last month that the boys be sent to a "specialised school", but did not elaborate. Under Chinese law, minors under 16 do not face criminal liability except in the case of major crimes like murder and rape.

Some reports suggest the boys filmed themselves and uploaded the video online, but police have not commented on that. Censors have tried to block the video to protect the boys' identity, although some people argue that it should stay.

Their identities have not been revealed, but snippets of the video with their faces visible continue to circulate online. There are also unverified posts claiming to be close-ups of the boys' faces, raising the risk of other children being wrongly identified.

Countries around the world restrict information about child offenders or set a high bar for identifying them.

For instance, media coverage and public access to juvenile court documents are often restricted to minimise psychological harm caused by undue publicity.

In this case, Chinese authorities have not completely banned the discussion yet. Keywords such as "Wang Wang" and "animal protection" came up as trending search terms on Monday, but posts related to them started to disappear towards the end of this week. Some users have also...
body.zh: 六月，当一段显示一只流浪狗及其幼犬惨遭杀害的视频在中国互联网上引发公愤时，北京的审查机器开始了行动。 但这次的不同寻常之处在于，震惊和愤怒的声音反对当局，当局表示他们担心涉案的四名男孩，他们都不满 14 岁。 中国共产党政权严格控制媒体和互联网，以压制对国家的批评并控制公众的愤怒。但在这起案件中，当局引用了男孩的年龄，敦促人们不要发表评论，并删除了有关该事件的社交媒体帖子。 官方声明称：“我们呼吁公众不要传播相关信息，拒绝网络欺凌，共同为未成年人成长创造良好环境。” 但这些限制似乎只会引发强烈抗议。中国的动物爱好者现在已经在线下和海外开展了斗争，甚至在纽约竖起了广告牌来争取支持。 在中国，事件发生三周后，有关该事件的帖子仍在社交媒体上吸引了数千条评论。人们感到震惊、愤怒和悲伤，也有人要求制定禁止虐待动物的法律，而中国目前还没有这样的法律。 六月底，一段令人不安的视频出现在网上，显示广东省揭阳市的男孩们用棍棒殴打三只小狗，然后放火焚烧它们的母亲。当这只名叫旺旺的狗被烧死时，男孩们在大笑。 揭阳当局上个月表示，这些男孩不会受到刑事指控，而是会被送往“特殊学校”，但没有详细说明。 一些报道称男孩们拍摄了自己并将视频上传到网上，但警方尚未对此发表评论。审查机构试图屏蔽该视频以保护男孩的身份，尽管有些人认为应该保留该视频。 他们的身份尚未透露，但可以看到他们脸部的视频片段仍在网上流传。还有未经证实的帖子声称是男孩脸部的特写，增加了其他孩子被错误识别的风险。 世界各国都限制有关儿童罪犯的信息，或为识别儿童罪犯设定了很高的标准。 例如，媒体报道和公众查阅少年法庭文件往往受到限制，以尽量减少不当宣传造成的心理伤害。 在这种情况下，中国当局还没有完全禁止讨论。 “旺旺”和“动物保护”等关键词成为周一的热门搜索词，但与它们相关的帖子在本周末开始消失。一些用户还报告说，他们分享他人帖子的能力受到了限制。 它...

reflection.en: The outrage over the killing of a dog and her puppies highlights a deep human impulse to defend the vulnerable. Even when voices are censored, the call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, like these voiceless creatures, resonates powerfully. This reminds us of the biblical mandate to advocate for the rights of all who are destitute and...
reflection.zh: 对一只狗及其幼崽被杀害的愤怒，凸显了人类保护弱者的深层冲动。即使声音被审查，为那些无法为自己发声的无声生灵说话的呼吁，依然强烈地回响。这提醒我们，圣经要求我们为所有贫困无助、无法自卫者的权利发声。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: ‘A statement of freedom’: T-shirt slogan goes viral and book sales rocket in Taiwan after Hong Kong raids
title.zh: 香港突袭后，台湾“自由宣言”T恤走红，书籍销量飙升

summary.en: Taiwanese citizens express concern over the situation of independent booksellers in Hong Kong following recent arrests. A woman's defiant walk from a bookstore, wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with a "statement of freedom," has gone viral, leading to increased book sales in Taiwan.
summary.zh: 近几个月香港独立书商遭到一系列逮捕后，台湾民众对他们的命运表示担忧。一名女子昂首走出香港一家仅存的独立书店，她T恤上印着的“自由宣言”标语走红，导致台湾的书籍销量飙升。

body.en: Taiwanese people look on with concern at fate of Hong Kong’s independent booksellers, after series of arrests in recent months Walking out of one of Hong Kong’s last remaining independent bookstores, hands behind her back but head held high, the woman’s T-shirt was emblazoned with a simple slogan : “I am a bookstore employee”. Escorted by police, the woman was among five people arrested during raids on two bookstores last week , suspected of displaying and selling publications with “seditious” content, a national security crime which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾民众对香港独立书商的命运表示担忧，经历了近几个月的一系列逮捕事件后，这名女子背着手，昂首阔步地走出香港仅存的一家独立书店，她的T恤上印着一句简单的标语：“我是书店员工”。在警方的护送下，这名女子是上周在两家书店突击搜查中被捕的五人之一，涉嫌展示和销售含有“煽动性”内容的出版物，这是一项国家安全犯罪，最高可判处 10 年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In times when truth is suppressed, the simple act of seeking and expressing it can become a powerful statement of freedom. Yahweh's word reminds us that knowing the truth is intrinsically linked to liberation, offering hope even amidst challenging circumstances. This story highlights the enduring human spirit that yearns for truth and the freedom it brings.
reflection.zh: 在真相被压制之时，寻求和表达真相的简单行为可以成为一种强大的自由宣言。雅伟的话语提醒我们，认识真理与获得自由是紧密相连的，即使在充满挑战的环境中也能带来希望。这个故事凸显了人类对真理及其所带来的自由的持久渴望。

verse.textEn: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
verse.textZh: 你们必晓得真理，真理必叫你们得以自由。

title.en: The Guardian view on Chinese workers picking up the pen: poetry in motion | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：中国工人拿起笔杆子，诗意盎然 | 社论

summary.en: A food delivery rider has won China's highest literary award, highlighting a growing trend of laborers engaging in creative writing. This phenomenon sheds light on the hundreds of millions who have built modern China, from street sweepers to factory workers and goods transporters, revealing their rich inner lives.
summary.zh: 一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖，这凸显了劳动者从事创意写作的日益增长的趋势。这一现象揭示了数亿建设现代中国的劳动者——从扫街工人到工厂员工和货物运输者——丰富的内心世界。

body.en: A food delivery rider has won the country’s highest literary award. It is part of a growing trend for writing by labourers The hundreds of millions who have built modern China from the ground up – sweeping its streets, labouring in its factories and ferrying its goods – are often overlooked. But they refuse to go unheard. Last week, a food delivery rider won China’s top literary award . Wang Jibing, 56, first caught attention when a poem about his experiences went viral in 2022. The following year, Hu Anyan’s memoir , I Deliver Parcels in Beijing, became a bestseller. In the early 20th century, Chinese intellectuals sought to capture the harsh realities of working-class lives. But it was under Mao Zedong that the idea of writing by as well as about the masses became reality, with labourers encouraged to take up the pen. In an era when the party tried to govern the language even of diaries and personal letters, the parameters of style and content were strict, and this enthusiasm swiftly diminished after Mao. But workers’ writing has seen a revival in the 21st century. This time, it is bottom-up rather than directed from above. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? body.zh: 一名送餐骑手获得了该国最高文学奖。这是劳动者写作日益增长的趋势的一部分。数以亿计白手起家建设现代中国的人——清扫街道、在工厂劳动、运送货物——常常被忽视。但他们拒绝被忽视。上周，一名外卖骑手荣获中国最高文学奖。 56 岁的王吉兵首次引起关注是在 2022 年，一首描写自己经历的诗在网上疯传。次年，胡安彦的回忆录《我在北京送包裹》成为畅销书。 20世纪初，中国知识分子试图捕捉工人阶级生活的严酷现实。但正是在毛泽东的领导下，由群众写作、为群众写作的理念才成为现实，并鼓励劳动者拿起笔来。在党试图控制日记和私人信件语言的时代，风格和内容的参数都很严格，这种热情在毛泽东之后迅速减弱。但工人写作在21世纪出现了复兴。这一次，它是自下而上的，而不是自上而下的。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that every person is Yahweh's handiwork, created with unique gifts and a purpose to do good works, often in ways that surprise us. It beautifully illustrates how creativity and dignity are not limited by one's occupation, but can flourish in any life dedicated to expressing its inherent worth.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，每个人都是雅伟的杰作，被赋予独特的恩赐和行善的目的，其方式常常出人意料。它优美地阐明了创造力和尊严并不受职业限制，而是在任何致力于表达其内在价值的生命中都能蓬勃发展。

verse.textEn: For we are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
verse.textZh: 我们原是他的工作，在基督耶稣里造成的，为要叫我们行善，就是神所预备叫我们行的。

title.en: Can India become the next semiconductor hub after Taiwan?
title.zh: 印度能否成为继台湾之后的下一个半导体中心？

summary.en: India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.
summary.zh: 随着主要工业强国寻求将供应链多元化，不再只依赖台湾，印度正投入数十亿美元建设国内半导体产业。

body.en:
India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry as major industrial powers seek to diversify supply chains beyond Taiwan.

More than 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are made in Taiwan , an island at the center of ongoing rivalry between the US and China .

Any disruption to Taiwan's chip industry would likely send shockwaves through the global economy, with modern semiconductors used to make everything from smartphones and electric vehicles (EVs) to aircraft and military systems .

During the COVID-19 pandemic, chip shortages forced automakers to halt production — exposing how dependent the world had become on a handful of manufacturers in East Asia.

The result has been a global race to build more resilient semiconductor supply chains. The US, Japan, South Korea and also the EU have all launched multi-billion-dollar programs to attract chipmakers.

India is now mounting its biggest push yet to become part of that network and enter the global arena as the next electronics powerhouse.

Last week, the Indian government approved a $13.2 billion (€11.4 billion) semiconductor program labeled Semicon 2.0. The project builds on the $9 billion India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched in 2021 and aims to develop the entire chip ecosystem — from chip design and fabrication to advanced packaging, specialty materials, equipment manufacturing and workforce training. 

Thousands of engineers working for companies such as Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments already design some of the world's most sophisticated chips from research centers in the Indian cities of Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Noida.

But analysts warn India has been lagging behind in large-scale manufacturing. In the semiconductor industry,  this is the area that brings both economic value and strategic importance.

"India already has the expertise to design sophisticated semiconductor chips," said V Kamakoti, director of the Indian Institute of Technology in the city of Madras.

"Indian engineers working for both domestic companies and multinational firms have successfully designed and delivered complex chips," Kamakoti told DW. "The bigger challenge is manufacturing them."

So far, India's progress has been concentrated in chip packaging and testing rather than manufacturing the chips themselves.

Kamakoti said the next step is building a domestic fabrication ecosystem that can turn those design strengths into large-scale production.

Micron Technology, a US memory chip maker, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi, two Indian semiconductor assembly and packaging companies, have begun commercial production under the first phase of India's semiconductor program.

summary.en: Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, expressing "strong concerns" and reiterating the importance of transparency following a recent ballistic missile test.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤与中国外长举行会晤，对近期弹道导弹试验表达了“强烈关切”，并重申了透明度的重要性。

body.en:
Australia has raised its concerns with China over its nuclear-capable missile test in the South Pacific, noting many of the region's nations also shared the same view.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong met with her Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, on the sidelines of ASEAN talks in the Philippines capital, Manila, on Tuesday evening.

"You speak about the importance of mutual understanding. I agree, and I expect we will discuss our concerns ... including around peace and stability in our region, safe and professional military conduct, and the importance of transparency and reassurance of intent," Wong said in opening remarks.

Wong noted the "strong concerns" expressed by many Pacific Island countries about the submarine-launched missile earlier in July.

The two foreign ministers also discussed the importance of peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

"You've often heard me say that we will cooperate where we can and disagree where we must, and we want to continue to engage because we believe that is in our national interest," Wong said.

Australia was only given a few hours' notice by China of the test, which was launched within hours of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese signing a new defence alliance with Fiji.

Albanese slammed the launch as a "provocative act" while other Pacific nations including New Zealand, Tuvalu and Fiji condemned the incident.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale was standing beside his Australian counterpart in his country's capital Honiara in early July when he said the test was "not the act of a friend".

Albanese has previously flagged a strong statement would be issued by the Pacific Islands Forum, but the group's disagreement on the wording of the text has resulted in a delay.

A foreign ministers' meeting of the forum will be held in August, where the issue is likely to be discussed.

body.en:
The relationship between police and Jewish community security groups came under scrutiny as the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion wrapped up its fifth hearing block in Melbourne.

Across five days, the inquiry heard evidence about the growing financial burden of security for Jewish Australians, police responses to antisemitic incidents, media coverage of the Hamas-Israel war and preparations for future hearings into last year's Bondi terror attack.

Today's hearings focused on the relationship between police and Jewish community security organisations, with Liberal MP Julian Leeser, Dor Foundation chief executive Tahli Blicblau, AFP assistant commissioner Stephen Nutt and Victoria Police assistant commissioner Martin O'Brien among those appearing before the commission.

The evidence is expected to help shape the commission's understanding of police data collection, security risk assessments and the role of emergency preparedness in responding to threats against the Jewish community.

Victoria Police also faced scrutiny over how antisemitic incidents are recorded. The commission heard an abusive phone call to a synagogue, in which the congregation was allegedly described as "genocidal" and "maggot rat Jews", was not recorded as a prejudice-motivated incident.

O'Brien confirmed no incident fact sheet had been logged for the call, which is required for any prejudice-motivated crime that relates to racial, political or ideological circumstances.

O'Brien said the force had "automatic scanning" every day of incidents, along with human analysts to consider threats.

A separate incident involving a 5.5m Nazi hakenkreuz symbol painted on a construction site was also not categorised under the relevant reporting system.

Security funding emerged as one of the dominant themes of the week's hearings, with Jewish community leaders telling the commission families, schools, places of worship and community organisations continue to bear much of the cost of keeping their communities safe.

On Thursday, the commission heard government funding since 2023 has covered about half of the security costs incurred by the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, which received $25 million to distribute to community organisations, places of worship and events.

Executive Council of Australian Jewry co-chief executive Peter Wertheim told the inquiry governments should ideally reimburse the council for all security costs it handles, while almost 200 organisations have applied for the latest federal funding allocation of $124 million over three years.

Socceroos star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine, after police stopped him while speeding over a bridge.

The 22-year-old, who represented Australia at the World Cup , was caught speeding twice overnight, NSW Police said on Friday.

Driving a BMW, Volpato was allegedly clocked at 109 km/h — nearly 50 km/h over the designated speed limit — when police stopped him on Sydney's Anzac Bridge at 1.10am on Friday.

He was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine, police said in a statement.

Volpato had earlier been stopped at 11.05pm on Thursday, police said, for travelling between 86 and 94km/h in a 60 zone.

Volpato returned a negative result when he was given the initial roadside breath test.

Volpato, who plays club football for Italian side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup.

He made headlines shortly before the tournament when he switched his international allegiance from Italy to Australia.

Volpato, who was born and raised in Sydney and played his junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney before moving overseas, represented Italy at U19 and U20 level.

The 22-year-old, who has scored seven goals in his three seasons with Sassuolo after two seasons with fellow Serie A club Roma, said in March he was "waiting for Italy" to select him for the senior side, who subsequently failed to qualify for the World Cup.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Deadly H5 bird flu appears to have reached Queensland's coastline for the first time as detections in wild seabirds across Australia climb to 17, sparking fresh warnings for vulnerable wildlife.

A deceased petrel found on Moreton Island returned an initial positive result for highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza at the Queensland government's Biosecurity Sciences Laboratory.

Samples have been sent to CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness for confirmatory testing.

Invasive Species Council policy director Carol Booth said the arrival of H5 bird flu in Queensland should alarm anybody concerned about Australia's native animals.

"Bird flu has now reached Queensland's coastline, and that should concern every Australian who cares about our wildlife," Booth said.

body.en:
Nearly five million Australians have been urged to stay vigilant for scams after a cyber attack on Origin Energy saw customer data accessed and disclosed.

Origin — Australia's largest energy retailer, with roughly 4.8 million customer accounts across electricity, gas, LPG and internet services — confirmed that names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information were all potentially viewed in the breach.

It said on Thursday it was working to understand how many of its customers were affected.

Also potentially exposed were the last four digits of credit cards and the last three digits of bank accounts.

That combination of data has raised the risk of follow-up scams, particularly phishing attempts that use real account details to appear more convincing.

Phishing scams involve fraudsters posing as a trusted organisation, often via email or text, to trick people into handing over personal details, passwords, or banking information.

But experts warn phishing may not be the only thing customers need to worry about.

New guidance from the company has urged customers to stay alert for scam emails and texts, designed to deceive people into providing their personal details.

"These fake emails often include a corporate logo and look like they've come from a legitimate company," Origin said.

Anyone who believes they've received a scam email is encouraged to report it to Scamwatch .

Origin has recommended customers keep a strong, unique password for their account and never share it with anyone, stressing it will never ask for a password over the phone or via email.

If a scam email arrives, the company's advice is to not click links, open attachments or forward it on, but to report it directly.

To tell a genuine email or text apart from a fake, Origin says to check for a suspicious sender address, spelling mistakes or bad grammar, and where any links actually lead.

"We've seen scam websites posing under originnergy.com.au so look carefully at the website address," Origin said, adding that the only safe way to pay a bill was via their website or the Origin app.

The company has also flagged fake job offers, and bogus calls or emails requesting orders or parts from people posing as Origin procurement staff, as scams to watch for.

Some experts say the breach is another example of a major company failing to handle a data incident well, and are calling for tough accountability standards for essential service providers.

The government has hit back at blanket new 12.5 per cent tariffs imposed by the United States on Australian goods, which came into effect on Friday.

The new permanent levy replaces a temporary 10 per cent tariff due to expire at the same time and is part of what the US claims is an effort to tackle the global issue of "forced labour" in supply chains.

Whilst the government insists its handling of forced labour and modern slavery is top-tier, one expert has said Australia's protections are greatly lacking, while another has suggested that Australia is a victim of Trump's tensions with China in this scenario.

Australian Trade Minister Don Farrell has called for the tariff measures to be reversed, telling SBS News that they are "unjustified" and "inconsistent" with existing free-trade agreements with the US.

Almost all goods sent to the US will be affected at the specific direction of US President Donald Trump.

Australia has increased its exports to the United States by 67 per cent since April 2025, when a blanket 10 per cent global tariff was applied on Trump's so-called "Liberation Day", Farrell said.

Primary exports to the US include beef, gold, wine, medical products, and various mining resources, the volume of which has increased dramatically, Farrell said, bringing the total value of the trading relationship to $1.32 trillion.

"Our largest exports to the United States continue to get into the United States tariff-free. What are they? It's beef, it's gold, and it's copper," Farrell told a press conference on Friday.

Australia is among 41 other economies the US trade department claims have failed to "impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced labor". These include Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Israel, Japan, Norway, Russia, and Singapore.

Other regions, which the US claims have also failed to "enforce" forced labour prohibitions, face a 10 per cent tariff. These include Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and Mexico.

The action is being taken against the US' 60 largest trading partners in an effort to "correct what is both a human rights abuse and a distortive trade practice to improve the welfare of workers everywhere".

title.en: Not a 'one off spike': Why higher petrol prices are set to return

summary.en: Multiple factors are expected to push up prices at the bowser, as markets also ramp up expectations for another rate hike.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Petrol prices are expected to rise once again, which could cause a crunch at the bowser for Australians already feeling the pinch.

While Australia's resilient labour market continues to be a bright spot in the nation's economy, including the addition of more than 76,000 jobs in June, dark clouds are gathering on the horizon.

After the Australian Bureau of Statistics released another strong labour force report on Thursday, bonds traders ratcheted up expectations that the Reserve Bank will raise interest rates for a fourth time in 2026.

The market is now full priced in for a rate hike by Christmas. A few weeks ago it was a 50-50 bet.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East have sent oil prices rising again and threaten to add fresh inflationary pressures to the economy.

While June quarter inflation data next week will be crucial to the RBA's next rates decision in August, the figures could already be dated by the time they are released.

Brent crude oil prices have risen from $US72 ($103) a barrel to more than $US96 ($138) a barrel in recent weeks.

As a rule of thumb, each dollar higher the benchmark oil price results in about a cent per litre increase in petrol prices at the bowser.

Along with an extra 16c a litre added to fuel prices from 2 August because of the full resumption of the federal excise , commuters could soon be looking at petrol prices above $2 a litre once more.

Australians might have to become accustomed to higher fuel prices sticking around, said economists at National Australia Bank.

"Recent developments in the Middle East show that the cost shock looks set to be less of a one-off spike and instead something that proves more grinding and protracted," they said in a research note.

Although jobs growth has remained robust, at 4.4 per cent the unemployment rate is higher than the RBA's June quarter forecast of 4.2 per cent, implying that the labour market is weaker than had been expected.

While higher oil prices risk pushing inflation higher, they also pose risks for growth, said Commonwealth Bank head of Australian economics Belinda Allen.

Victoria's economy is leading the way down, where the state's unemployment rate climbed to 5.1 per cent.

title.en: Australia’s winter wonderland is becoming increasingly reliant on a backup plan

summary.en: An unpredictable season is testing the measures resorts rely on when the snow does not arrive as hoped.

body.en:
As the sun rises over Mount Buller in Victoria's High Country, the hum of snow guns echoes across the mountain, blanketing ski runs in artificial snow.

As winters become less predictable, operators are investing heavily in snowmaking technology, effectively an insurance policy keeping lifts turning and visitors coming when natural snowfall falls short.

With little natural snow falling until 3 July, one of the slowest starts to winter in decades, several resorts still managed to turn lifts on the traditional June long weekend opening thanks to artificial snowmaking — even if only thin stripes of beginner's terrain were open.

Among them was Mount Buller, which has invested $17 million in snowmaking in the past 25 years.

The resort now operates more than 300 snow guns across almost 80km of ski runs, which can generally operate only at a wet-bulb temperature of -2C or below.

Mount Buller also has five snow factories — shipping container-like buildings capable of producing snow around the clock, regardless of temperature.

"Snowmaking has progressively become more and more significant around the world because it smooths out the variability from season to season," Mount Buller spokesperson Rhylla Morgan told SBS News.

"We haven't had many of those big snow events yet. There have only been a handful so far this season, so snowmaking helps us fill in those gaps.

"It allows us to maintain snow cover across the ski area and steadily build that base, which has enabled us to progressively open more terrain and keep our guests skiing and snowboarding."

Morgan said snowmaking technology — which is both water-and energy-intensive — had improved significantly in the decades since its introduction, allowing resorts to produce higher-quality snow more efficiently.

"The technology has really become very finessed; there are amazing companies around the world working to improve that every year," she said.

Resorts also rely on "snow farming" to extend their seasons by creating snow stockpiles in south-facing and shaded areas, which are then groomed to top up runs.

She said Australia's ski industry — which supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes billions of dollars to the economy — was continuously adapting to the changing climate.

While snowmaking has helped resorts cope with poor natural conditions, it hasn't changed the weather.

After an early July dump of snow, the Spencers Creek measuring site — considered the most reliable site for natural snow depth in NSW — recorded a depth of 68cm on 21 July. A good year would exceed a metre.

title.en: Origin Energy reports customer bank, credit card details caught up in data breach
title.zh: Origin Energy报告客户银行和信用卡详细信息在数据泄露中被盗

summary.en: Origin Energy has confirmed that customer bank and credit card details were compromised in a recent data breach. The company had initially reported being affected by a breach earlier in the week, and has now disclosed the full extent of the stolen information.
